column1: 315|R|Arthur Koestler|1959|1687|0|0|14,11,8,7,8,9,6,3.5,3,1.5|Astronomical ideas are linked to scientists' beliefs and historical context. Strong narrative contrasts can overstate psychological explanations; scientific history remains valuable without technical derivations.

316|R|Bill Mesler; H. James Cleaves II|2015||0|0|17,12,9,9,8,8,5,4,2.5,1.5|Origin-of-life debates connect experiments, assumptions and changing standards of evidence. Broad history supplies useful uncertainty lessons without a laboratory curriculum.

317|R|Henry M. Cowles|2020|1910|0|0|18,12,10,9,8,9,5,4.5,2.5,1.5|The scientific-method idea is traced through evolution, psychology and education. Intellectual history tests a familiar simplification rather than prescribing a technical method.

319|R|John North|2005|1336|0|0|18,12,8,9,7.5,9,7,5,2,1.5|Richard of Wallingford's clock connects astronomy, instruments and institutions. Explanatory biography qualifies, although specialist reconstruction lowers general-reader yield and the topic incurs maximum historical age.

320|R|Seb Falk|2020|1400|0|0|18,13,9,9,8.5,9,6,4.5,3,1.5|Medieval instruments and scholarship connect calculation, navigation and monastic networks. Concrete practices challenge simplistic dark-age narratives; historical endpoint is approximate.

321|R|Toby E. Huff|2011|1700|0|0|15,14,10,9,7.5,8,6,4,2.5,1.5|Comparative responses to instruments link institutions and scientific inquiry. Civilizational comparisons risk uneven evidence and overgeneralization; no allegiance-based veto is presumed.

322|R|Toby E. Huff|1993|1700|0|0|15,14,10,9,7.5,9,6,4,2.5,1.5|Legal and educational institutions are proposed as conditions for early modern science. Broad cross-cultural causal claims need counterexamples and receive qualified integrity credit.

323|R|James A. Brundage|2008|1500|0|0|18,10,7,8,7.5,9,3,5,2,1.5|Legal-profession formation connects training, courts and institutional authority. Historical explanation qualifies, but administrative detail and low technology fit limit priority.

324|R|Isaac Asimov|1966||0|0|16,9,6,7,8,7,5,4,3,1.5|Cosmological history explains successive models and observations. Historical exposition survives, but obsolete contemporary astronomy and familiar basics reduce current value.

325|R|Johnjoe McFadden|2021||0|0|15,12,9,8,7.5,8,5,4,3,1.5|Occam's razor connects explanatory economy and scientific change. A single organizing principle can over-simplify historical causation; examples still add learning.

326|R|Luke Heaton|2015||0|0|17,12,9,9,8,9,7,4,2.5,1.5|Number, calculus, infinity and computation are situated in human problems. The publisher and contents establish explanatory history; speculative prehistory limits confidence in early claims.

327|R|Alexandre Koyré|1957|1700|0|0|18,11,8,8,8,9,6,5,2,1.5|Cosmological change connects metaphysical assumptions and mathematical physics. Close intellectual history offers distinctions, with less emphasis on instruments and institutions.

328|R|Albert Einstein; Leopold Infeld|1938||0|0|17,10,8,9,8,9,5,5,3,2|Conceptual transitions from classical to modern physics are explained without specialist derivations. Historical reasoning remains useful, but much content is elementary for this reader.

329|R|David M. Bressoud|2019|1900|0|0|18,10,8,9,8,9,7,5,2.5,1.5|Calculus's historical order is contrasted with modern teaching sequences. Explanatory development rather than a full calculus curriculum supplies the main value.

330|E|Jim Baggott||||||OUP identifies a senior undergraduate/graduate guide for quantum courses, with formal practice, Bell-theorem arguments and tests. Specialist quantum-study purpose triggers hard exclusion.

331|R|Ivar Ekeland|2006||0|0|17,12,10,9,8,9,6,4.5,2.5,1.5|Optimization links physical principles, economics and social choice. Conceptual explanation offers transfer without a specialist optimization course; analogy across domains needs caution.

332|R|Francis Spufford|2003|2000|-10|0|17,13,11,9,8.5,9,7,4,3,2|British technical projects connect ingenuity, industry and changing institutions. Distinct cases add mechanisms; national framing earns T11 without nullifying the engineering value.

333|R|Oliver Sacks|2001|1950|0|0|17,10,7,8,8,9,5,4.5,3,2|Scientific childhood connects materials, experiments and conceptual discovery. Memoir provides learning and scientific biography value, though introductory chemistry limits novelty.

334|R|A. F. Chalmers|1976||0|-10|18,10,9,8,8,9,4,4.5,2.5,1.5|Competing accounts of scientific knowledge expose induction, testing and theory-choice problems. Conceptual philosophy is not technical training, but philosophy is central.

335|R|Morris Kline|1953|1915|0|0|17,13,8,9,8,9,6,4.5,2.5,1.5|Mathematics is explained through cultural and scientific influence. Historical synthesis qualifies; dated historiography and broad generalizations constrain integrity.

336|R|Morris Kline|1959||0|0|17,12,8,9,8,9,6,4.5,2.5,1.5|Mathematical ideas are explained through the physical problems they address. General-reader explanatory purpose qualifies, while elementary derivations offer limited novelty for a physicist.

337|R|Carl Zimmer|2001||0|0|18,12,8,9,8.5,8,4,4.5,3,1.5|Evolutionary mechanisms are linked to historical evidence and biological cases. Strong explanatory biology has indirect strategic fit and some dated coverage.

338|R|John Carey (editor)|1995||0|0|17,10,7,6,8,9,5,4,3,2|Scientific writing from different periods adds observations, discoveries and explanatory styles. Anthology variety increases knowledge but not necessarily causal integration.

339|R|John Carey (editor)|1987||0|0|16,7,5,4,7.5,9,2,4,3,2|Eyewitness accounts provide vivid primary observations across history. Selection and witness limitations require context; strategic mechanisms are not the organizing purpose.

340|R|E. J. Dijksterhuis|1950|1700|0|0|19,13,9,10,8,9,7,5,2,1.5|Mechanical explanation develops through astronomy, mathematics and physical theory. Scholarly synthesis qualifies despite technical demands; historical treatment needs modern historiographic context.

341|R|Paul Feyerabend|2011||0|-10|13,9,7,6,7,8,3,4,2.5,1.5|Lectures criticize scientific authority and universal method claims. Useful counterexamples coexist with polemical overreach; methodological philosophy is central.

342|R|Roger G. Newton|2004||0|0|17,11,8,8,8,9,6,4.5,2.5,1.5|Pendulum science connects measurement, mathematical models and experimental control. Historical mechanisms qualify without training the reader in specialist procedures.

343|R|Roger G. Newton|2007||0|0|18,12,8,9,8,9,6,4.5,2.5,1.5|Physics history contrasts deterministic models and probability. Conceptual development is durable, though much technical content is familiar to this reader.

344|R|Richard DeWitt|2004||0|-10|17,11,8,8,7.5,8,4,4,2.5,1.5|Scientific worldviews connect evidence, theories and philosophical commitments. A history/philosophy textbook is not automatically a technical curriculum; conceptual analysis supplies the main value.

345|R|Peter J. Bowler; Iwan Rhys Morus|2005||0|0|19,14,10,10,8,9,6,5,2.5,1.5|Modern science connects disciplines, institutions and social settings. A survey used in teaching still qualifies when its main value is explanatory history rather than technical proficiency.

346|R|Iwan Rhys Morus (editor)|2002||0|0|17,12,8,8,7.5,8,5,4.5,2,1.5|Historical essays connect bodily models, machines and scientific practice. Comparative perspectives offer insight, with uneven argument and density across contributions.

347|R|J. R. Partington|1937|1930|0|0|18,10,7,8,8,9,6,5,2,1.5|Chemical discoveries are traced through experiments and concepts. Historical survey qualifies, though older scholarship and specialist detail reduce present learning efficiency.

348|R|David Park|2005||0|0|17,12,8,8,7.5,8,5,4.5,2.5,1.5|Changing accounts of the cosmos connect religion, physical theory and culture. Broad intellectual history is explanatory rather than doctrinal; synthesis can compress disagreements.

349|R|Stillman Drake|1978|1642|0|0|19,11,9,10,8.5,9,7,5,2,1.5|Galileo's working sequence links experiment, mathematical argument and publication. Documentary scientific biography qualifies even with demanding technical context.

350|R|Chris McDonald|2021|1960|0|0|16,13,10,9,8,9,7,3.5,2.5,1.5|The switch connects telegraph relays, electronic computation and semiconductors. Author-published history with accessible original chapters gives mechanisms; independent scholarly validation is limited.
